Let $x=ai+bj+ck$, where $a,b,c\in\mathbb R$. Using $i^2=j^2=k^2=-1$ and the anticommutativity of $i,j,k$, the mixed terms cancel, giving
\[
x^2=-(a^2+b^2+c^2).
\]
Thus $x^2=-1$ precisely when $a^2+b^2+c^2=1$. The unit sphere in $\mathbb R^3$ contains infinitely many points; for example, every
\[
(a,b,c)=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta,0),\qquad \theta\in\mathbb R,
\]
produces a solution. Hence there are infinitely many quaternionic solutions.
\end{proof}
